source.verification_operation: Search official repository for ExactlyOnceKafkaWriter recovery implementation, then exact-fetch the implementation file at the FE-503 pinned commit.

finding.summary: The recovered-writer lingering-transaction cleanup seen in FE-503 is triggered synchronously by writer initialization, not by an autonomous no-writer reconciler in ExactlyOnceKafkaWriter. initialize() calls abortLingeringTransactions(recoveredStates, restoredCheckpointId + 1) before starting the next transaction. abortLingeringTransactions builds a TransactionAbortStrategyContext and invokes transactionAbortStrategy.abortTransactions(context). The supplied aborter obtains a transactional producer; the implementation comment states that getTransactionalProducer already calls initTransactions, which cancels the transaction. close() separately invokes abortCurrentProducer() only for the current producer when it has records. The class therefore exposes recovery-time initialization and orderly close as cleanup entry points, but no timer/background path that can execute while the writer/job is absent.
falsifying_trace: Prior state exists from a previous execution.
A new ExactlyOnceKafkaWriter is constructed/restored and initialize() runs.
The abort strategy receives an aborter whose producer acquisition calls initTransactions and cancels the targeted transaction.
If neither a writer initialization/recovery nor close path executes, this class contains no autonomous trigger that invokes the lingering-transaction cleanup.
finding.scope_guard: Only ExactlyOnceKafkaWriter.java at apache/flink-connector-kafka commit dc707db60fcf3c0637114503c27685c881519c2c. This proves the trigger location and lack of an autonomous trigger inside this class only. It does not prove absence of broker-side expiration, another Flink component, or autonomous logic inside TransactionAbortStrategyImpl; those remain untested here.
finding.no_restart_no_close_status: unresolved_outside_this_class; within this class cleanup requires initialize/recovery or close entry points
